findings.title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
findings.body: The denial key uses only the parsed subject ID, discarding IdentityType even though permission lookup distinguishes anonymous, renderer, and user identities. For example, `anonymous:0` and `render:0` produce the same denial key for the same dashboard request. If the anonymous request is denied first, the renderer request is also denied for 30 seconds without reaching getRendererPermissions, which would grant dashboard read access. Include the identity type in the key to prevent denials from crossing identity boundaries.

findings.title: Encode denial-key components without delimiter collisions
findings.body: Concatenating resource name and parent with unescaped underscores allows different requests to share a denial key. For the same namespace, subject, and action, name `foo_bar` with parent `baz` collides with name `foo` and parent `bar_baz`. Underscores are supported in legacy dashboard/folder UIDs, and request validation does not exclude them. A denial for one resource can therefore incorrectly deny access to another resource for the cache TTL. Use an unambiguous encoding of the components.

findings.title: Seed an actual grant in the denial-precedence test
findings.body: The test says it grants dashboard access to prove that the denial entry takes precedence, but it stores `"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`. checkPermission treats that entry as a denial, so this does not test the intended conflict between a cached grant and a cached denial. Set the entry to true so the test verifies that a denial-cache hit overrides an otherwise allowed request.
